findings.text: Exposes a global helper that performs a synchronous cross-CPU rendezvous after page-table removal. It is explicitly weaker than a grace period and is presented as sufficient only for software walkers that rely on interrupt masking.

Exposes a global PMD collapse helper that requires a PMD-aligned address on a non-huge entry, atomically takes and clears the entry, invalidates the whole huge range for normal page-table entries, and returns the previous entry.

The collapse control carries at least a daemon-versus-direct flag, per-node load counters, a node allocation mask, and a present-entry bitmap for multi-size attempts. Fault descriptors for swap-in are built with owning area, faulting address, file offset derived from address, retry-allowed flags, and the PMD slot.

Isolation succeeds only when the observed reference count matches the expected count and LRU isolation succeeds; otherwise the folio is unlocked and a distinct count or LRU outcome is reported. Successfully isolated folios are accounted as isolated, must remain locked and off the LRU, large ones are queued separately, and daemon scans additionally require at least one referenced entry or fail with a dedicated lack-of-reference outcome.

Successful copy handling walks every small slot in the target range, counts empty slots as anonymous, drops zero mappings through a KSM hook, and for mapped slots removes table entries and reverse mappings under the table lock before releasing swap cache and references with batching for large folios. Queued compound folios are afterwards unlinked, unaccounted, unlocked, and returned to reclaim.

Copy failure first reinstalls the original table pointer under the PMD lock while isolated pages stay locked, then releases both raw and compound isolated pages. Ordering keeps table restoration before page release and avoids needing the higher-level area lock at that point.

Per-page copying zeroes destinations for empty or zero entries and otherwise copies from the mapped source with a poison-aware routine; any poison indication aborts the loop with a dedicated copy outcome and routes to failure handling, while a clean walk routes to success handling.

Allocation sleep waits interruptibly and freezably on a daemon queue for a tunable millisecond interval. The daemon control defaults to daemon mode. Allocation strength selects full hugepage reclaim when a defragmentation flag bit is set and a lighter form otherwise; direct collapses always use the full form.

Node suitability veto applies only when reclaim-based locality is enabled and the candidate node has no recorded load; it then rejects the node when any loaded node lies beyond a configured distance. Nodes with existing load are never vetoed.

Target selection chooses the lowest-numbered node with the highest recorded load and marks every online node tied at that maximum in the allocation mask. A second build variant without node awareness always selects node zero.

Revalidation rejects exiting or disabled owners, missing areas, areas not spanning a full PMD at the aligned address, orders not allowed for the caller type, and unexpected non-anonymous remaps when anon was expected. Caller type derives from daemon versus direct mode.

PMD examination reports missing tables for empty, non-present, or malformed entries and reports already-mapped for migration entries and established huge mappings; only a present non-huge well-formed table passes. A still-valid check re-resolves the PMD and fails when the slot address changed.

Swap-in walks the target range slot by slot under read protection, skipping empty and present entries and faulting only swapped entries. Non-PMD orders are rejected with a swap-tolerance outcome instead of faulting. Retry responses are treated as page-lock failures without retry, error responses fail, and any brought-in pages trigger a reclaim-cache drain.

Charged allocation first allocates the requested order on the selected node under the computed mask, records allocation success or failure statistics, then charges the owner group; charge failure frees the folio and reports a group-charge outcome. PMD orders add an extra group event count.

Anonymous collapse allocates and charges before taking locks, validates area and PMD under read protection with optional swap-in, then revalidates under write protection, marks the area for write, rechecks PMD identity, and only then takes the area write lock, issues a clear notification over exactly the modified range, flushes the PMD, ends notification, and synchronizes tables before attempting isolation.

Multi-size scanning walks a PMD-sized window in aligned strides, skipping disabled orders. Each candidate counts present entries from a bitmap plus swapped entries for the PMD candidate, compares against an order-specific empty tolerance, and attempts collapse only when occupancy is sufficient. The next order after each stride is capped by trailing alignment of the new offset.

Candidate outcomes split three ways: success and already-huge advance past the candidate stride; allocation, reference, tolerance, page-state, and entry-state setbacks record the outcome and retry the same offset at a smaller enabled order; already-mapped PMD and any other outcome record and stop the scan. Final status prefers any success over allocation failure over the last setback.

Installation after successful isolation and copy marks the new folio current with ordering before table publication, requires the PMD slot to be empty, then diverges: PMD order deposits the old table and installs a PMD mapping, while smaller orders repopulate the table and install batched PTE mappings with write-protect cleared. Area write protection is released early only for PMD order and otherwise held across copy and install.

Anonymous collapse orchestration is the lane-local entry that turns a start address, reference and unmapped hints, control block, and order into a scan outcome, owning allocation, validation, notification, isolation, copy, and installation, with tracing of success and outcome.

Ordering is read protection for initial checks, then write protection, then area start-write marking, then area write lock, then notifier bracketing around PMD lock with flush, then table lock for isolation and copy. The distinct PTE lock is nested inside the PMD lock only when reinstalling tables for smaller orders on architectures needing a live hierarchy.

The PTE table lock serializes clearing entries, reverse-map removal, and statistics updates during success handling, and is held across isolation with explicit release on both paths. The PMD lock serializes clearing with flush and both restore paths, and failure restoration holds it while isolated pages remain locked.

Hazards include poisoned sources aborting copy, migration entries masquerading as mappable PMDs, shared-PMD races when an area does not span the full PMD, coexisting huge and small translations without a flush, swap faults dropping read protection and forcing no-lock exit, retry and error fault codes needing distinct handling, and swap-in potentially enabling later higher-order collapses.

Order and size identities derive from PMD order with page count as one shifted by order and range length as page size scaled by that count; PMD alignment uses a dedicated mask and PMD span a dedicated size. Defragmentation selection tests a dedicated flag bit in global huge-page flags, and allocation strength toggles between full and light huge variants on that test.
